## Density ratio estimation

Many statistical learning problems can be solved through a density ratio:

$$
r(x) = \frac{p_\text{nu}(x)}{p_\text{de}(x)}
$$

- Reweighing: covariate shift / sample selection bias

- Anomaly detection

- Two-sample testing

- Classification

## Estimating the density ratio

Divergence minimization ([Sugiyama et al. (2012)](https://doi.org/10.1007/s10463-011-0343-8))

$$
BR_f(r||\hat r) = \int \Big(
    f(r(x)) - f(\hat r(x)) - f'(\hat r(x))(r(x) - \hat r(x))
\Big) p_\text{de}(x) \text d x
$$

where $f(t)$ is a differentiable and strictly convex function with derivative $f'(t)$

- UKL: $f(t) = t \log t - t$; Least-squares: $f(t) = (t-1)^2/2$.

And $\hat r(x)$ a model for the density ratio, typically linear and kernel-based; $\hat r(x) = \psi(x) \theta$.

## {background-iframe="https://thomvolker.github.io/densityratio/"}

## The `densityratio` R-package

Implements a suite of methods for density ratio estimation, with:

- A unified interface
- Automatic model selection through cross-validation (in parallel)
- Estimation in `C++`
- Helper functions for two-sample testing and visualization

## Example 1: Covariate shift

```{r}
#| label: preliminaries
#| echo: false

library(densityratio)
set.seed(123)
idx <- insurance$region %in% c("southwest", "southeast")
data <- subset(insurance, select = -region)

south <- subset(data, subset = idx)
south_x <- subset(south, select = -charges)
north <- subset(data, subset = !idx)
north_x <- subset(north, select = -charges)
```

Insurance data from U.S.

- Variables: age, sex, bmi, number of children, smoker, charges
- Training data: data from the south
- Deployment data: data from the north

__Goal__: Predict insurance charges in northern region from model trained on southern region

- Reweight loss by importance weights $r(x) = \frac{p_\text{north}(x)}{p_\text{south}(x)}$

## Density ratio estimation for distribution shift

```{r}
#| label: dr-estimation
#| echo: true


dr <- ulsif(
    df_numerator = north_x, 
    df_denominator = south_x, 
    nsigma = 20, 
    nlambda = 20, 
    nthreads = 10
)

summary(dr)
```

## Inspecting the density ratio

```{r}
#| label: dr-plot
#| echo: true

plot(dr)
```

## xgboost prediction with importance weights



```{r}
#| label: get-weights
#| echo: true

weights <- predict(dr, newdata = south_x)

fit_cs <- xgboost::xgboost(
    x = model.matrix(~., south_x), 
    y = south$charges,
    weights = c(weights)
)
```

:::{.fragment}
```{r}

fit <- xgboost::xgboost(
    x = model.matrix(~., south_x), 
    y = south$charges
)

mse_unw_south <- mean((south$charges - predict(fit, newdata = model.matrix(~.,south_x)))^2)
mse_w_south <- mean((south$charges - predict(fit_cs, newdata = model.matrix(~.,south_x)))^2)

mse_unw_north <- mean((north$charges - predict(fit, newdata = model.matrix(~.,north_x)))^2)
mse_w_north <- mean((north$charges - predict(fit_cs, newdata = model.matrix(~.,north_x)))^2)

tibble::tibble(
    " " = c("RMSE Unweighted", "RMSE Weighted"),
    "South (train)" = c(
        sqrt(mse_unw_south), sqrt(mse_w_south)
    ),
    "North (test)" = c(
        sqrt(mse_unw_north), sqrt(mse_w_north)
    )
) |> knitr::kable()
```

:::

## Example 2: Two sample testing

Colon data: 2000 gene expression measurements from 22 colon tumor tissues, and 40 non-tumor tissues.

__Goal__: Evaluate whether two groups have significantly different gene expression measurements.

- Exploit connection between DR estimation and divergence estimation between $p_\text{nu}(x)$ and $p_\text{de}(x)$.


```{r}
colon <- subset(densityratio::colon, class == "tumor", select = -class)
healthy <- subset(densityratio::colon, class == "normal", select = -class)
```

## Density ratio estimation with dimension reduction

```{r}
#| label: spectral
#| echo: true
dr <- spectral(colon, healthy)
plot(dr)
```

## Two-sample testing with density-ratios {.smaller}

Permutation test: compare observed divergence to distribution of null divergences under random reallocation

```{r}
#| label: test-two-sample
#| echo: true
#| cache: true


summary(dr, test = TRUE, cl = 12)
```
